chapter: Records, Lovie Austin and a first marriage
title: 1922 sides, Fletcher Henderson, and the Original Memphis Five
summary: She does not recall recording with Sam Wooding; she says she was the first Black woman to record with a white band, the Original Memphis Five, and introduced Porter Grainger's "'Tain't Nobody's Business".

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, you did -- did you -- do you remember ever recording with Sam Wooding's orchestra?

Because you did some -- two sides in 1922 in New York, in September of '22 -- You Can't Have It All and Lonesome Monday Morning Blues. And the record collectors seem to think that it may be Sam Wooding's
Orchestra, but nobody really knows who was accompanying you then.

"Lonesome Monday Morning Blues." Let me see. Who could that be? I don't ever remember having recorded with Sam Wooding. I don't remember. But I know I used to record with Fletcher a lot. I used to record with -- let me see. What other band was that I recorded with that had --
-- Eubie, yes, Eubie, but most of my --
Oh, yes, I wanted to remember that. I was the first Negro girl to record with a white band. And they were superb. They were wonderful, Chris.
And that's when you recorded 'Tain't Nobody's Business.
Business -- that's Porter Grainger's song. Porter Grainger wrote that. And I introduced it. See?
That's right, and that was on the same session you did "Bleeding Hearted Blues" and "If You Want to Keep Your Daddy Home."
Well, Lovie must have -- Lovie must have played that. No, no, Lovie didn't do that.
